generation.explanation: A Riemann sum approximates the area under a curve by slicing the region into n thin rectangles and adding up their areas, each with width Δx = 2/n and height f(xᵢ) = xᵢ² at a chosen sample point. Since x² is increasing, right endpoints overestimate the area while left endpoints underestimate it — and the true value ∫₀² x² dx = 8/3 ≈ 2.667 is trapped between them. Drag the slider to increase n and watch the sum converge to 8/3 as the error shrinks toward zero. Use the checkbox to switch between right and left endpoints to see the over- vs. under-estimation.
